guided.note: Issue #64's guided-discovery axis, from TestGuidedSweepAgainstFloci (go test -run TestGuidedSweepAgainstFloci, TF_FLOCI_TEST=1). cold_calls is the estate-wide sweep's API call count over sweep_types with Request.Guided false; guided_routine_calls is the same sweep with Request.Guided true and a fresh record-store hint (aws_sns_topic present, aws_kms_key and aws_route53_zone absent); guided_verify_calls adds Request.GuidedVerify, which must match cold_calls exactly. The config-driven scan costs nothing in any of the three numbers -- aws_s3_bucket is client-named and never reaches Discover's list/bind machinery, see assertBucketsCostNothing -- so every call counted here belongs to the sweep alone. This is not a ratchet: TestGuidedSweepAgainstFloci's own assertions (guided_routine_calls < cold_calls, guided_verify_calls == cold_calls) are the gate; this section only keeps the artifact's numbers current with the most recent measurement.

note: Issue #64's committed call-count budget. Generated by internal/live/discovery.TestPlanCallBudgetAgainstFloci (go test -run TestPlanCallBudgetAgainstFloci, TF_FLOCI_TEST=1), which reads this file back and fails if a fresh measurement at the same n exceeds calls_total by more than tolerance. calls_total covers discovery.Discover plus projection.BuildFrom for an N=200 aws_s3_bucket estate (tools/estate-gen -count 200) with no prior state - the read cost live-plan pays end to end, not just the discovery/list half. wall_clock_bucket and measured_at are informational only, never gated: floci's performance on whatever machine runs the test, not this repository's code, is what a wall-clock assertion would actually be grading. calls_by_api's per-bucket shape (~17 calls/instance: 3 HEAD /{bucket} plus one GET per S3 subresource the aws_s3_bucket Read covers - acl, cors, encryption, lifecycle, logging, object-lock, policy, replication, requestPayment, versioning, website, accelerate - plus 2 more folded into 'GET /{bucket}/...', which is this proxy's catch-all for any deeper-path or S3-Control-routed call such as bucket tags) is a property of the AWS provider's own aws_s3_bucket Read, not of anything this fork adds; it is recorded here as the baseline this ratchet protects, not as a target to optimize down. This artifact's second measurement (2026-08-13, merging issue #60's parent-read sweep on top of issue #64's own baseline) adds four new per-bucket GETs the first measurement did not pay: encryption, lifecycle, policy and versioning each double from one GET (the aws_s3_bucket Read's own subresource fetch) to two (a second, independent list of the matching aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration / aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration / aws_s3_bucket_policy / aws_s3_bucket_versioning parent-read child), and publicAccessBlock appears for the first time at one per bucket (aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block has no Read-time analog on aws_s3_bucket itself, only the parent-read child) — the same untaggable-child-via-parent-read discovery issue #60 adds, at the O(N) cost the leg is supposed to pay once the accidental O(N^2) an initial merge of that leg carried (internal/live/discovery/parent_read.go's per-parent unscoped-list loop, fixed the same day) is corrected. See internal/live/discovery/scale_bench_test.go's doc comment for the full method, and internal/live/cloudcontrol/doc.go's 'Retries' section for the backoff policy issue #64 asked for. This artifact's scope was checked again on 2026-08-21, when GitHub issue #349's root-output data-read class added a fourth kind of pre-plan cloud call (one ReadDataSource per data BLOCK a root-level output block reaches, shared across that block's instances, best-effort and never retried): it does not move calls_total, and it is not silently outside the ratchet either. Two independent reasons, both checked rather than assumed. First, TestPlanCallBudgetAgainstFloci counts what discovery.Discover and projection.BuildFrom send, and the new phase runs in the command layer (internal/command/live_plan.go's statelessRootOutputDataReads) beside them, not inside either. Second, and the reason widening the measurement would still read 0: the estate this ratchet is measured over is generated by tools/estate-gen, which emits no root-level output blocks at all, so the phase's demand walk finds nothing to read. An estate whose outputs DO reach data sources pays one call per such block, once, on top of the per-instance read cost above - the same price stock OpenTofu pays for the same blocks on every plan. This artifact's third measurement (2026-08-30, issue #563, re-run at the current pin ghcr.io/lex00/floci@sha256:c55d74e1... after several pin moves this artifact had fallen behind - see live/flociimage_test.go's staleFlociMeasurements) found the per-bucket shape and its 22-call/instance slope completely unchanged (N=20: 453 calls; N=200: 4413 calls; N=1000: 22013 calls, all three exactly fitting calls_total = 22*N + 13 with no residual - see internal/live/discovery/scale_bench_test.go's TestScaleAgainstFloci run at ESTATE_BENCH_N=20 and 1000 alongside this file's own N=200). What moved is the fixed, N-independent term alone: three new one-off calls appear at this pin that did not appear at sha256:4753246c - AmazonEC2ContainerRegistry_V20150921.DescribeRepositories, one extra top-level 'GET /{bucket}', and secretsmanager.ListSecrets - taking the constant term from 10 calls to 13 (calls_total was 22*N + 10 at the prior pin, exactly; see the git history of this file). Read as evidence for #546's O(types)-not-O(resources) claim, this is confirmation rather than erosion: the three new calls are account/service-level probes that fire once regardless of N, not once per resource, so as N grows their share of calls_total keeps shrinking (13/453 = 2.9% of the total at N=20, 13/22013 = 0.06% at N=1000) exactly the way a true O(1) term should. The O(N) slope this ratchet exists to catch a regression in is untouched.
wall_clock_bucket: single digit to tens of seconds depending on N (this measurement: apply 9.8s / plan 8.2s at N=200, apply 22.9s / plan 44.3s at N=1000, measured locally against floci on the machine that recorded this artifact)
